measured.and_the_symbol_change_is_not_free: Binding the loop to POSITION_START also changed the reduced vehicle's PREFILL token from 1126 to 2284, so the loop descriptor is load-bearing for prefill addressing too.
measured.both_numbers_are_137_but_from_different_: That is the whole difficulty.  Bind the single loop to CONTEXT_LENGTH and the output reads 9 + 129 = 138 against operands of 137.  Bind it to POSITION_START and the output reads 8 + 129 = 137 while the operand clamps to 8 and the operands sum to 136.  Measured both ways, one build each.
measured.the_decode_output_extent: RequestAxis(POSITION_START, unit=1, numerator=1, bias=129).  _phase_substitution rewrites the extent across section 12.2's relation -- context_length = position_start + span_tokens -- so pinning span_tokens to 1 turns the context form into POSITION_START + 1, and the committed window's 128 plus that 1 is the bias of 129.  At decode POSITION_START is 8, so 8 + 129 = 137.
measured.the_operand_axis: context_length itself, identity, bias 0.  At decode CONTEXT_LENGTH is 9, so the compressed prefix holds 9 rows and with the 128-row window the operands sum to 137.

not_a_claim: the two-loop design is reasoned from two measurements, not implemented
state_of_the_tree: Reverted to the two GATED fixes.  The reduced V4.1 array rebuilds byte-identically to the gated build (695b4f30...), V4-Flash and Qwen3 are unmoved from the A18 baseline, and the ratio-2 join passes decode while the ratio-1 join does not.
the_last_structural_fact: The join's OUTPUT extent and its context-derived OPERAND need loops bound to DIFFERENT symbols, so one loop per kernel cannot resolve both.
what_the_complete_fix_needs: TWO loops per phase-split join: one bound to the symbol the output's extent names, one to the symbol the context operand's own axis names
per-phase INPUT views, so the decode form reads the operand's capacity while prefill reads its token block (implemented and measured: operands 129 -> 137)
and a V4-Flash token re-walk, because per-phase input views move its digest (0e7cc36b... -> 176c24ed...)
why_I_stopped_here: Each step of this sequence revealed the next layer, and the last two attempts regressed prefill -- the token flipping to 2284 twice is the signal that I was changing a load-bearing descriptor faster than I was establishing what depends on it.  Two loops plus per-phase inputs plus a re-walk of a closed cell is a coherent piece of work and not a fifth incremental edit, and leaving the tree at a gated state is worth more than leaving it mid-sequence.
